content: Tetracycline hydrochloride is a yellow, odorless, crystalline powder. It remains stable when exposed to air; however, prolonged exposure to strong sunlight causes it to darken. The compound's potency is compromised in solutions with a pH below 2 and is rapidly degraded in the presence of alkaline hydroxide solutions. Tetracycline is only very slightly soluble in water. It dissolves freely in dilute acid and alkaline hydroxide solutions, sparingly in alcohol, and is practically insoluble in chloroform and ether. The chemical name of tetracycline hydrochloride is 4-(Dimethylamino)-1,4,4a,5,5a,6,11,12a-octahydro-3,6,10,12,12a-pentahydroxy-6-methyl-1,11-dioxo-2-naphthacenecarboxamide monohydrochloride. Each capsule, intended for oral administration, contains either 250 mg or 500 mg of tetracycline hydrochloride. The inactive ingredients in the formulation include lactose, light mineral oil, and magnesium stearate. The capsule shells for both the 250 mg and 500 mg doses are composed of D&C Yellow No. 10, FD&C Blue No. 1, FD&C Yellow No. 6, gelatin, and titanium dioxide. The imprinting ink used on the capsules contains D&C Yellow No. 10, FD&C Blue No. 1, FD&C Blue No. 2, FD&C Red No. 40, black iron oxide, pharmaceutical shellac glaze, propylene glycol, and n-butyl alcohol.
